name: Emergence of Classes: memory and the way out of fractiousness (Fig. 4)
description: Axtell, Epstein and Young's Fig. 4: from a fractious start (every memory half H, half L), 10 agents; the metric is the first period at which every agent holds at least (1 − ε)·m M's (their transition target), capped at 100 000. They report exponential growth with memory — over 10⁵ periods at m = 13. Measured (release, seeds 1–10, recorded 2026-09-25): at ε = 0.05, 992, 391, 1060, 49 500 (one run capped) and 21 900 periods at m = 6, 8, 10, 12, 14; at ε = 0.1, 228, 416, 168, 1420, 1506. It grows, unevenly (at ε = 0.05 every memory from 6 to 14 must be all M; at ε = 0.1 rounding makes m = 6 and 8 demand an all-M memory too), and two orders of magnitude below the paper's.
